newsitem.title: GERMANY: Puma Q1 profit up but shareholders wary.
newsitem.headline: Puma Q1 profit up but shareholders wary.

text.p: Puma AG said on Thursday sales and profits rose in the first quarter and dismissed shareholder worries that the German sportswear group was striving too hard for record profits.

Puma said pre-tax profit for the quarter rose to 30.6 million marks ($17.8 million) from 27.7 million marks in the 1996 first quarter while net sales rose 3.6 percent to 153.6 million marks from 148.3 million marks in the year-ago period.

Puma chief executive Jochen Zeitz told the group's annual shareholder meeting that Puma was poised for a fourth consecutive year of record profit as the group strengthens its return to health after near-bankruptcy in the early 1990s.

He also said Puma was aiming to pay a higher dividend in the near-term to shareholders who had endured stumbles by the group in the past before it revamped its image and product lines and re-established its competitiveness.

The group last year reported a gain in sales to 489.9 million marks from 413.6 million and a near doubling in net profit to 83.8 million marks from 48.2 million marks in 1995. Pre-tax profit was up 25 percent at 64.86 million marks.

One shareholder told the meeting Puma must stop relying on extraordinary items to report higher profits, while another said the explosive growth cannot be sustained since "a tree does not endlessly grow into the heavens".
"You have put the bar up very high and hopefully you can spring over it," one shareholder told the Puma management board about what he called ambitious goals.
Zeitz said the fears were ungrounded. Puma had no plans for takeovers and was not worried that it might be the object of a takeover.
He also noted that operating profits - a sign of the group's financial health - was up 6.4 percent in the first quarter to 153.6 million marks.
